meta.title: Residential Parking Permit Portal — software requirements specification
meta.idPolicy: Identifiers were frozen at gate G4. Withdrawn identifiers are not reused. Design and test add their own columns and do not renumber these rows.

introduction.purpose: This software requirements specification is the proposed baseline for design, build, and test of the Residential Parking Permit Portal. It tells the sponsor what will be held as requirements and tells later agents which decisions they must not make. It is not an approved handoff until a named person records approval.
introduction.scope: The product lets a resident apply for one vehicle, prove an eligible address, pay the current ordinance fee after a clerk approves, and receive a permit an officer can check by plate without seeing personal details. Topics the sponsor excluded are out of scope. Topics the sponsor left open are open questions, not defaults. A topic in neither list is not a requirement.
introduction.productPerspective: Residents sign in with a one-time email link and do not receive a city password. Clerks sign in through the city single sign-on. The portal sends the resident to CityPay for card entry, sends three notices through CityNotify, and answers a lookup the enforcement handheld will call. Parking Services supplies the cleaned address list and the current fees as data. No other external party is in the source.
productFunctions: Record one application for one vehicle and accept submission only when the address and the file pass (FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004).
Let a parking clerk approve or reject a submitted application (FR-005, FR-006).
Show the current fee, take payment on CityPay, and issue an Active permit (FR-007, FR-008, FR-009, FR-010).
Email the resident at submission, rejection, and issuance (FR-011, FR-012).
Start a renewal inside the stated window from the current permit (FR-013).
Suspend or revoke with a reason code, and keep that permit off Active lookups (FR-014, FR-015).
Answer a plate lookup with zone, status, and expiry only (FR-019, FR-020).
userCharacteristics: Residents were not in the working session. The sponsor said they do not get a city network account (STK-001).
Parking clerks use the city sign-on and decide applications and permit status under the stated rules (STK-002).
Enforcement officers use the existing handheld and do not review applications (STK-003).
Finance reconciles references and amounts and does not use the portal day to day (STK-004).
The accessibility coordinator and the privacy officer were named as reviewers and were not interviewed. They have no quotations in the source (STK-005, STK-006).
Dana Okonkwo was interviewed and accepts or rejects scope (STK-007). Interest and influence values elsewhere in the register are analyst judgments or are unknown.
limitations: Visitor, temporary, and commercial permits, citations, appeals, meter payment, electric-vehicle-only bays, address overrides, a household cap, and post-expiry renewal are Won't (SC-OUT-01 through SC-OUT-07).
Open questions OQ-001 through OQ-007 are unanswered. Downstream work must not invent those decisions.
Handheld representation and clerk sign-on token format are deferred to design inside the business data already stated.
No assumption was required. Where a fact was missing, a question was raised instead.

stakeholders.name: Resident
stakeholders.role: Applies, pays, and renews. Does not receive a city network account.
concerns: Needs to obtain a permit and pay online instead of queueing at the counter (BRD §2, BRD §3).

stakeholders.name: Parking clerk
stakeholders.role: Reviews applications and suspends or revokes permits, using the city sign-on.
concerns: Reviews proof and decides Submitted applications (BRD §4, BRD §6.5, BRD §6.6).
stakeholders.decisionRights: May approve or reject a Submitted application and may suspend or revoke an Active permit under the stated rules (BRD §6.5, BRD §6.6, BRD §6.8).

stakeholders.name: Enforcement officer
stakeholders.role: Looks a plate up from the existing handheld. Does not review applications.
concerns: Needs permit zone, status, and expiry without the resident's personal details (BRD §2, BRD §6.11).

stakeholders.name: Finance
stakeholders.role: Reconciles CityPay collections. Does not use the portal day to day.
concerns: Needs the CityPay reference and the amount reported as paid (BRD §4, BRD §6.12).

stakeholders.name: Accessibility coordinator
stakeholders.role: Named reviewer of POL-ACC-01. Was not in the working session.
concerns: Named as a reviewer of POL-ACC-01. No statement from this person is in the source (BRD §4).

stakeholders.name: Privacy officer
stakeholders.role: Named reviewer of the cited privacy-related policies. Was not in the working session.
concerns: Named as a reviewer. No statement from this person is in the source (BRD §4).

stakeholders.name: Dana Okonkwo
stakeholders.role: Parking Services Manager and sponsor of this request.
concerns: Wants residents to apply and pay online and officers to check a plate without hearing personal details (BRD §2).
stakeholders.decisionRights: Accepts or rejects scope for this request (BRD §4).

needs.statement: A resident of an eligible address needs a one-year permission to park one stated vehicle without coming to the counter.
The resident needs to pay the published fee for that permission, and finance needs the CityPay reference and amount.
An enforcement officer needs a plate's permit zone, status, and expiry without receiving the resident's name, address, email, or proof-of-address file.
A resident who holds an Active permit needs to start a renewal inside the stated window without retyping the stored name, address, plate, and jurisdiction.
A parking clerk needs to stop an Active permit from being treated as valid when eligibility has lapsed or fraud has been found, and needs that decision recorded.
A resident needs to complete application entry, file upload, and the CityPay handoff on a phone and under the accessibility and browser policies the sponsor cited.
The resident's proof-of-address file and payment card data need to stay with the people and the processor the sponsor named.
The sponsor needs monthly counts of permits issued, permits expired, and fees collected, grouped by zone, and will still open the resident service if this slips.
A resident needs to sign in by proving control of an email address, without a city-issued password.
A clerk's authority needs to come from the city single sign-on group parking-clerk, not from an account this product invents.

inScope.item: Online application for a resident, one vehicle per application.
One proof-of-address file on that application.
Clerk decision to approve or reject a submitted application.
Payment of the annual fee through CityPay after approval.
Renewal inside the window in BRD §6.7.
Officer lookup by plate and jurisdiction.
Email at submission, rejection, and issuance.
Monthly totals by zone, which the sponsor allows to slip to the next increment.

outOfScope.item: Visitor permits, temporary permits, and commercial permits.
outOfScope.rationale: The sponsor said these are not this project (BRD §5).
The handheld already does citations. The sponsor excluded appeals (BRD §5).
The sponsor said this is not decided and told the project to leave it out until she says otherwise (BRD §5).

outOfScope.item: A clerk override that approves an address which is not on the eligible-address list.
outOfScope.rationale: The sponsor said not to build an override until she decides (BRD §5).

outOfScope.item: A household cap on how many Active permits one household may hold.
outOfScope.rationale: The sponsor said the policy is unwritten and not to pick a number (BRD §5). The unanswered policy is also OQ-001, so design does not invent a cap while this baseline excludes one.

outOfScope.item: Renewal after the expiry date, including any grace period.
outOfScope.rationale: The sponsor limited renewal to the window in BRD §6.7 and said this project does not include a renewal after expiry (BRD §5).

dependencies.statement: CityPay hosts the card page and, on success, reports a payment reference and the amount paid.
CityNotify is the mail relay used for the submission, rejection, and issuance emails.
The city single sign-on can assert the group parking-clerk for a clerk.
Parking Services supplies the cleaned eligible-address list for each zone.
The handheld team will call the lookup. They will specify representation in design.

constraints.statement: Do not add fuzzy matching. Compare the entered street address to the cleaned list.
Do not store the card number or the card security code. Collect them only on the CityPay page.
Do not invent the handheld wire format. Representation is a design decision constrained by the lookup business content.
A zone fee and the eligible-address list must be changeable without a software release.
Submission time and audit time are recorded in UTC.

requirements.statement: The portal shall record, on one application by an authenticated resident, a legal name, a residential street address, an email address, one license plate, and that plate's jurisdiction.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.1.

acceptanceCriteria.title: One application holds the sourced fields and one plate
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an authenticated resident
When the resident records a legal name, a residential street address, an email address, one license plate, and a jurisdiction on an application
Then the application contains those values
And the application does not contain a second license plate

acceptanceCriteria.title: A missing jurisdiction is not a complete application
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an authenticated resident who has not recorded a jurisdiction
When the resident tries to treat the application as complete
Then the portal does not treat the application as containing the required set of fields

requirements.rationale: BRD §6.1 treats these fields as the contents of one application, so they stay one completeness rule. A second plate, a household limit, and guest permits are not added: the first is contrary to this rule, and the others are SC-OUT-06, OQ-001, and SC-OUT-01.

requirements.statement: The portal shall refuse submission of an application whose residential street address is not on the eligible-address list Parking Services supplied for that application's zone.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.3.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Sponsor's own example address is refused
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given the eligible-address list for zone R-A contains 100 Market Street
And that list does not contain 9 Dock Lane
When a resident tries to submit an application for zone R-A at 9 Dock Lane
Then the portal refuses submission
And the application does not become Submitted

acceptanceCriteria.title: An address on the list is not refused by this rule
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given the eligible-address list for zone R-A contains 100 Market Street
When a resident submits an otherwise complete application for zone R-A at 100 Market Street
Then this address rule does not refuse the submission

requirements.rationale: The comparison is against the cleaned list the sponsor will supply. Fuzzy matching is forbidden by CON-001. A clerk override is SC-OUT-05. Which upstream system produces the list is OQ-002 and is not decided here.

requirements.statement: The portal shall accept submission only when the application has exactly one proof-of-address file whose media type is PDF, JPEG, or PNG and whose size is no greater than 10 megabytes.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.4.

acceptanceCriteria.title: One PNG at the stated cap satisfies the file rule
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application with no proof-of-address file yet
When the resident attaches one PNG file of 10 megabytes
Then the file rule is satisfied for that application

acceptanceCriteria.title: A file over the cap is refused
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application
When the resident attaches one PNG file larger than 10 megabytes
Then the portal does not accept submission on the strength of that file

acceptanceCriteria.title: A second file is refused
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application that already has one PDF proof-of-address file
When the resident attaches a second file
Then the portal does not accept submission with two proof-of-address files

requirements.rationale: The file rule is the sponsor's list and size cap. Who may later retrieve the file is NFR-005. How long the file is kept is OQ-003 and is not given a period here.

requirements.statement: The portal shall record an accepted submission as status Submitted, with the submission time in UTC, on the clerk review queue.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.6.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A passing submission joins the queue
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application that has passed the address rule and the file rule
When the resident submits it
Then the status is Submitted
And the submission time is recorded in UTC
And the application is on the clerk review queue

requirements.rationale: Accepted means the address rule and the file rule already passed. Draft applications are not on the queue, which is the sponsor's state model in BRD §6.6, not an extra workflow.

requirements.statement: The portal shall let a user in the parking-clerk role change an application from status Submitted to status Approved.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.6.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A clerk approves a submitted application
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
And an application in status Submitted
When the clerk approves it
Then the application status is Approved

acceptanceCriteria.title: A draft is not approved from the queue
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
And an application in status Draft
When the clerk looks for it on the review queue
Then the application is not on the queue and is not changed to Approved

requirements.rationale: Approval is a clerk action on a Submitted application. The sponsor did not define a clerk override for an address off the list, so this statement does not add one (SC-OUT-05).

requirements.statement: The portal shall let a user in the parking-clerk role change an application from status Submitted to status Rejected only when that user supplies a reason at least 15 characters long.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.5.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Fifteen characters rejects
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
And an application in status Submitted
When the clerk rejects it with a reason of 15 characters
Then the application status is Rejected
And the reason is retained

acceptanceCriteria.title: Fourteen characters does not reject
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
And an application in status Submitted
When the clerk tries to reject it with a reason of 14 characters
Then the application status remains Submitted

requirements.rationale: The 15-character floor is the sponsor's work rule. A shorter reason leaves the application Submitted, which BRD §6.5 states directly.

requirements.statement: The portal shall show the current ordinance fee for the application's zone, in US dollars, immediately before the resident is sent to pay.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.2.

acceptanceCriteria.title: The shown amount is the current zone fee
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given the current fee for zone R-A is 60 US dollars
And the current fee for zone R-B is 90 US dollars
When the resident is about to be sent to pay an Approved application for zone R-B
Then the portal shows 90 US dollars
And the resident has not yet been sent to CityPay

requirements.rationale: The fee is the current card amount at the moment of handoff, not a copy frozen at submission, because BRD §6.2 says the amount shown and the amount sent are the current fee at that moment. The card values are data, not hard-coded shall text, so an ordinance change does not require a new requirement.

requirements.statement: The portal shall send the resident to the CityPay hosted page for an application only when that application is Approved.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.6.

acceptanceCriteria.title: An approved application can be handed to CityPay
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application in status Approved
When the resident continues to payment
Then the portal sends the resident to the CityPay hosted page for that application

acceptanceCriteria.title: A submitted application is not handed to CityPay
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application in status Submitted
When the resident tries to pay
Then the portal does not send the resident to the CityPay hosted page

requirements.rationale: Payment before approval is excluded by the sponsor's sequence. Card capture itself is NFR-006 and stays on CityPay's page.

requirements.statement: The portal shall record the CityPay payment reference and the amount CityPay reported when CityPay reports that the fee was paid successfully.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.6.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A success report is stored
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an Approved application whose current fee was shown as 60 US dollars
When CityPay reports success with a payment reference and an amount of 60 US dollars
Then the portal records that reference and that amount against the application

acceptanceCriteria.title: No success report means no successful payment
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an Approved application
When CityPay has not reported success
Then the portal has no successful payment recorded for that application

requirements.rationale: The portal records the reference and the amount the processor reports. It does not record the card number. Absence of a success report is not turned into a success by a timeout the sponsor did not state.

requirements.statement: The portal shall issue a new permit in status Active, with a permit number the portal has not issued before and with an expiry date 365 days after the issue date, only when the linked application is Approved and a successful CityPay payment is recorded for it.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.6.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Approval plus payment issues a new Active permit
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an Approved application with a successful CityPay payment recorded
When the portal issues the permit
Then the new permit is Active
And its permit number has not been issued before
And its expiry date is 365 days after its issue date

acceptanceCriteria.title: Approval without payment does not issue
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an Approved application with no successful CityPay payment recorded
When issuance is considered
Then the portal does not create an Active permit for that application

requirements.rationale: Issuance is the same gate for a first application and for a renewal. BRD §6.7 says a renewal issues a new permit and leaves the previous permit unchanged. This statement does not shorten the previous permit and does not add a grace period (SC-OUT-07).

requirements.statement: The portal shall send one email through CityNotify to the application's email address when the application becomes Submitted, when it becomes Rejected, and when a permit is issued for it.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.9.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Submission sends one email
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application that has just become Submitted
When the portal sends the submission notice
Then one email is sent through CityNotify to the email address on the application

acceptanceCriteria.title: Rejection sends one email
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an application that has just become Rejected
When the portal sends the rejection notice
Then one email is sent through CityNotify to the email address on the application

acceptanceCriteria.title: Issuance sends one email
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a permit that has just been issued for an application
When the portal sends the issuance notice
Then one email is sent through CityNotify to the email address on the application

requirements.rationale: The three events are the sponsor's list. The one-time sign-in link is a different send (FR-017). The source does not say that link uses CityNotify, so this statement does not attach it. That channel is OQ-007.

requirements.statement: The portal shall record a failed CityNotify attempt, stop after 3 attempts for that event, and leave the application or permit status unchanged when CityNotify does not accept the message.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.9.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A refused message does not undo issuance
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a permit that has just been issued
When CityNotify does not accept the issuance message
Then the portal records the failed attempt
And the permit remains issued

acceptanceCriteria.title: Attempts stop at three
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an event whose CityNotify message has already failed 3 times
When the portal considers another attempt for that same event
Then the portal does not send a fourth attempt

requirements.rationale: BRD §6.9 binds the record, the cap of 3, and the refusal to undo the business action as one failure behavior. Clerks phoning the resident is outside the product and is not turned into a shall.

requirements.statement: The portal shall let a resident authenticated with the email address on an Active permit start a renewal application on or after the date 45 days before that permit's expiry date and on or before that expiry date, prefilled with that permit's legal name, residential street address, license plate, and jurisdiction.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.7.

acceptanceCriteria.title: The window opens on day 45 and prefills the four fields
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an Active permit whose expiry date is 45 days after the current date
And a resident authenticated with the email address on that permit
When the resident starts a renewal
Then the portal creates a renewal application
And that application is prefilled with that permit's legal name, residential street address, license plate, and jurisdiction

acceptanceCriteria.title: A day earlier than the window does not start a renewal
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given an Active permit whose expiry date is 46 days after the current date
And a resident authenticated with the email address on that permit
When the resident tries to start a renewal
Then the portal does not create a renewal application

requirements.rationale: The window bounds are the sponsor's, inclusive of day 45 and of the expiry date. A different email cannot start that renewal. After expiry is SC-OUT-07, not a late-renewal shall.

requirements.statement: The portal shall change a permit from Active to Suspended or from Active to Revoked only when a user in the parking-clerk role records a reason code of eligibility-lapsed, non-payment, fraud, or other.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.8.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A listed reason code suspends
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
And a permit in status Active
When the clerk suspends it with reason code eligibility-lapsed
Then the permit status is Suspended
And the reason code is retained

acceptanceCriteria.title: A missing reason code does not revoke
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
And a permit in status Active
When the clerk tries to revoke it without a reason code
Then the permit status remains Active

requirements.rationale: The four reason codes are the sponsor's closed list. Lookup consequences are FR-015, not a second copy of this decision.

requirements.statement: The portal shall report a lookup status of Active only when the matched permit is stored as Active and the lookup date is on or before that permit's expiry date.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.8.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A current Active permit is reported Active
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a permit stored as Active whose expiry date is on or after the lookup date
When a plate lookup matches that permit
Then the reported status is Active

acceptanceCriteria.title: Suspended, revoked, and past expiry are not Active
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a plate lookup that matches a permit stored as Suspended
When the same kind of lookup is repeated for a permit stored as Revoked and for a permit whose expiry date is before the lookup date
Then none of those three results reports status Active

requirements.rationale: Suspended, Revoked, a date after expiry, and not-found are all outside Active, by BRD §6.8 and §6.11. The statement does not invent a stored status called Expired. The report counts expiry dates separately (FR-016).

requirements.statement: The portal shall produce, for a calendar month it is given, the count of permits whose issue date falls in that month, the count of permits whose expiry date falls in that month, and the sum of successful CityPay amounts recorded in that month, each grouped by zone.
requirements.priorityRationale: BRD §3 says the sponsor will still open the service to residents if the monthly totals slip to the next increment.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Fixture records roll up by the stated definitions
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a calendar month in which zone R-A has one permit with an issue date in the month, one permit with an expiry date in the month, and successful CityPay payments totaling 60 US dollars
And zone R-B has none of those
When the figures for that month are produced
Then zone R-A shows 1 issued, 1 expired, and 60 US dollars
And zone R-B shows 0 issued, 0 expired, and 0 US dollars

requirements.rationale: The three aggregations are defined by BRD §6.14. Who is allowed to request the report is OQ-006, so this statement names no role. Priority is Should because the sponsor will open the resident service even if the report slips.

requirements.statement: The portal shall start a resident session only after the resident opens a one-time link that the portal sent to the email address the resident entered.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.10.

acceptanceCriteria.title: The link starts a session
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a resident who entered an email address
And a one-time link the portal sent to that address
When the resident opens the link
Then the portal starts a resident session for that email address

acceptanceCriteria.title: No link means no session
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a resident who entered an email address
When the resident has not opened a one-time link sent to that address
Then the portal does not start a resident session

requirements.rationale: The sponsor forbade a city password for residents. The channel that carries the link is not named and is OQ-007. This statement does not assume CityNotify.

requirements.statement: The portal shall start a parking-clerk session only when a city single sign-on asserts the group parking-clerk.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.10.

acceptanceCriteria.title: The group starts a clerk session
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a city single sign-on that asserts the group parking-clerk
When the portal establishes the session
Then the session is a parking-clerk session

acceptanceCriteria.title: A sign-on without the group does not start a clerk session
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a city single sign-on that does not assert the group parking-clerk
When the portal considers a clerk session
Then the portal does not start a parking-clerk session

requirements.rationale: The group claim is the sponsor's rule. Token format and protocol are not specified and stay deferred to design under CON-003's sibling constraint for representation, recorded on IF-004.

requirements.statement: The portal shall answer a plate-and-jurisdiction lookup with the matching permit's zone, status, and expiry date, or with a not-found result when no permit matches that plate and jurisdiction.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.11.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A matching plate returns zone, status, and expiry
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a permit for plate ABC123 in a jurisdiction, with a zone and an expiry date
When a lookup asks for plate ABC123 and that jurisdiction
Then the result contains that zone, the permit status, and that expiry date

acceptanceCriteria.title: An unknown plate is not-found
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given no permit for plate ZZZ999 and the requested jurisdiction
When a lookup asks for that plate and jurisdiction
Then the result is not-found
And the result is not an Active permit

requirements.rationale: The response business content is fixed here. The wire format is deferred to design (CON-003, IF-003). Not-found is a normal result, not an error code invented by this specification.

requirements.statement: The portal shall omit the resident's legal name, residential street address, email address, and proof-of-address file from every plate-lookup response.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.4.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A hit omits personal details and the file
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a permit that matches the requested plate and jurisdiction
When the lookup response is returned
Then the response does not contain the resident's legal name, residential street address, email address, or proof-of-address file

requirements.rationale: This is the sponsor's replacement for the office reading personal details over the phone. It does not prescribe encryption or a token scheme.

requirements.statement: The portal shall return a plate-lookup response within 2 seconds for at least 95 percent of lookups when 50 authenticated lookup clients call the lookup at the same time.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.11.

acceptanceCriteria.title: The sourced load meets the sourced time
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given 50 authenticated lookup clients calling the plate lookup at the same time
When the responses are measured
Then at least 95 percent of those responses are returned within 2 seconds

requirements.rationale: Scale is lookup response time, the meter is the share of lookups observed at the portal under the stated concurrency, and the target is the captain's figure as Dana recorded it. No resident-page budget is copied from this number. That gap is OQ-004.

requirements.statement: The portal shall let a resident complete application entry, proof-of-address upload, and the handoff to CityPay at a viewport width of 360 CSS pixels without horizontal scrolling.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §7.

acceptanceCriteria.title: The three named tasks fit the stated width
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a viewport 360 CSS pixels wide
When a resident completes application entry, proof-of-address upload, and the handoff to CityPay
Then none of those tasks requires horizontal scrolling

requirements.rationale: The width and the three tasks are what the sponsor stated from POL-ACC-01. No other breakpoint is added.

requirements.statement: The portal shall conform the resident flows and the clerk flows to WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §7.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Named flows are inspected against the cited level
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given the resident flows and the clerk flows
When those flows are inspected against WCAG 2.2 Level AA
Then each flow conforms to that level

requirements.rationale: The sponsor cited WCAG 2.2 Level AA for resident and clerk flows and did not attach the rest of POL-ACC-01. This shall is that citation, not a private selection of success criteria. The accessibility coordinator was not in the room and is not quoted.

requirements.statement: The portal shall present the resident flows in the current major version and the immediately previous major version of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §7.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Each named browser at both stated generations presents the resident flows
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given the current major version and the immediately previous major version of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge
When a resident uses each of those versions for the resident flows
Then the resident flows are presented in each of those versions

requirements.rationale: POL-BROWSER-02 as the sponsor stated it. No other browser and no clerk-flow browser matrix is added, because the sponsor applied this policy to resident flows.

requirements.statement: The portal shall let a proof-of-address file be retrieved only by the resident who uploaded it and by a user in the parking-clerk role.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.4.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Clerk and uploading resident can retrieve the file
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a proof-of-address file uploaded by a resident
When that resident retrieves it and a user in the parking-clerk role retrieves it
Then both retrievals are allowed

acceptanceCriteria.title: Another resident cannot retrieve the file
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a proof-of-address file uploaded by one resident
When a different resident tries to retrieve it
Then the portal does not return the file

requirements.rationale: The allowed people are the sponsor's list. The statement does not choose storage encryption, a document-management product, or a retention period (OQ-003).

requirements.statement: The portal shall keep payment card numbers and card security codes out of portal storage by collecting them only on the CityPay hosted page.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.12.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Card entry is on CityPay and the values are not stored
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a resident paying an Approved application
When the resident enters a card number and a card security code
Then that entry happens on the CityPay hosted page
And the portal has not stored the card number or the card security code

requirements.rationale: POL-SEC-04 as the sponsor applied it. No card-vault product and no cipher suite is named.

requirements.statement: The portal shall keep the resident flows and the plate lookup available for at least 99.5 percent of the minutes in each calendar month outside maintenance windows published at least 48 hours before they start.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §7.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Monthly minutes meet the stated percentage
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a calendar month and the maintenance windows that were published at least 48 hours before they started
When available minutes of the resident flows and of the plate lookup are divided by the minutes in that month outside those windows
Then the result is at least 99.5 percent

requirements.rationale: The percentage, the month, the two surfaces, and the 48-hour notice are POL-AVAIL-03 as stated. Restore time after an unplanned outage is not in the policy sentence and is OQ-005.

requirements.statement: The portal shall apply an update to a zone's current fee or to the eligible-address list without a software release.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.2.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A fee change is visible without a release
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given zone R-A has a current fee of 60 US dollars
When that current fee is updated to 70 US dollars without a software release
Then an Approved R-A application handed to payment after the update shows 70 US dollars

acceptanceCriteria.title: An address-list change is applied without a release
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given 9 Dock Lane is not on the zone R-A eligible-address list
When 9 Dock Lane is added to that list without a software release
Then a later submission for zone R-A at 9 Dock Lane is not refused by the address rule

requirements.rationale: The sponsor required ordinance changes to take effect without a release. Who types the update is not stated, so no editor role is added. Provenance of the address list remains OQ-002.

requirements.statement: The portal shall append an audit record containing the actor, the time in UTC, and the reason or the payment reference for each approval, rejection, issuance, suspension, and revocation.
requirements.priorityRationale: The sponsor stated this as behavior of this request, not as an optional later increment. BRD §6.13.

acceptanceCriteria.title: A revocation writes the sourced audit fields
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a user in the parking-clerk role
When that user revokes an Active permit with reason code fraud
Then an audit record is appended with that actor, the time in UTC, and the reason code

acceptanceCriteria.title: Issuance records the payment reference
acceptanceCriteria.gherkin:
Given a successful CityPay payment reference on an Approved application
When the portal issues the permit
Then an audit record is appended with the actor, the time in UTC, and that payment reference

requirements.rationale: The five actions and the three fields are the sponsor's audit rule. No log product is named.

useCases.name: Apply for a residential permit
preconditions: A resident session has been started under FR-017.

mainSuccessScenario.step: The resident records the application fields and one plate.
The address is on the eligible-address list for the zone.
Exactly one allowed proof-of-address file is attached.
Submission is recorded as Submitted on the clerk queue.

extensions.condition: The address is not on the list for the zone.
extensions.behavior: Submission is refused and the application does not become Submitted.

extensions.condition: The file is missing, is a second file, is the wrong media type, or is larger than 10 megabytes.

useCases.name: Review an application
preconditions: A parking-clerk session has been started under FR-018.
useCases.trigger: The clerk takes a Submitted application from the review queue.

mainSuccessScenario.step: The clerk changes the application from Submitted to Approved.

extensions.condition: The clerk rejects with a reason at least 15 characters long.
extensions.behavior: The application becomes Rejected and the reason is kept.

extensions.condition: The reason is shorter than 15 characters.

useCases.name: Pay and receive a permit
useCases.trigger: The resident continues an Approved application to payment.

mainSuccessScenario.step: The current zone fee is shown.
The resident is sent to the CityPay hosted page.
A successful CityPay report is recorded.
A new Active permit is issued.
An issuance email is sent through CityNotify.

extensions.behavior: No successful payment is recorded and no Active permit is issued.

useCases.name: Renew a permit
preconditions: The resident is authenticated with the email address on the Active permit.
The current date is inside the renewal window.

mainSuccessScenario.step: A renewal application is created and prefilled from the current permit.
After approval, payment and issuance follow the same rules as a first application.

extensions.condition: The current date is before the window.

useCases.name: Look up a plate
preconditions: The lookup is requested by an authenticated lookup client.
useCases.trigger: A plate and jurisdiction are presented.

mainSuccessScenario.step: The response carries zone, status, and expiry, or not-found.
Active is reported only for a stored Active permit still inside its expiry date.
Personal details and the proof file are omitted.

extensions.condition: Nothing matches the plate and jurisdiction.
extensions.behavior: The result is not-found and is not Active.

useCases.name: Suspend or revoke a permit
preconditions: A parking-clerk session has been started.
useCases.trigger: The clerk records a reason code against the permit.

mainSuccessScenario.step: The permit becomes Suspended or Revoked and the reason code is kept.

extensions.condition: A later lookup matches that permit.
extensions.behavior: The lookup does not report Active.

userStories.iWant: to record one plate and the application fields on a single application
userStories.soThat: I can ask for a street permit without queueing at the counter

userStories.iWant: submission refused when my street address is not on the zone list
userStories.soThat: an ineligible address does not become a submitted application

userStories.iWant: to attach one proof-of-address file within the stated type and size limits
userStories.soThat: the clerk can review the proof the sponsor required

userStories.iWant: to approve a submitted application or reject it with a reason of at least 15 characters
userStories.soThat: only a completed review moves the application on

userStories.iWant: to see the current zone fee and be sent to CityPay only after approval
userStories.soThat: I pay the ordinance amount through the city's processor

userStories.iWant: a new Active permit only after approval and a successful payment
userStories.soThat: an officer can verify a permit that has actually been paid

userStories.iWant: an email through CityNotify when I submit, when I am rejected, and when a permit is issued
userStories.soThat: I hear the outcomes the sponsor required

userStories.iWant: to start a renewal from my Active permit inside the stated window, with my stored details prefilled
userStories.soThat: I do not retype the name, address, plate, and jurisdiction

userStories.iWant: the monthly counts and fee totals defined for each zone

interfaces.name: CityPay payment
interfaces.purpose: Collect the current zone fee after approval and return the processor's success report.
dataSent: Current fee amount in US dollars
interfaces.errorBehavior: If CityPay does not report success, the portal records no successful payment and does not issue a permit.
interfaces.representation: The source mandates CityPay's hosted card page. Any further message format is deferred to design and may not add card storage.

interfaces.name: CityNotify resident email
interfaces.purpose: Send the submission, rejection, and issuance notices to the application email address.
dataSent: Event: Submitted, Rejected, or permit issued
interfaces.errorBehavior: Record the failure, send at most 3 attempts for that event, and do not change the application or permit status because the message failed.
interfaces.representation: Deferred to design. The source names CityNotify and the business content only. This interface does not carry the one-time sign-in link (OQ-007).

interfaces.name: Enforcement plate lookup
interfaces.purpose: Answer a plate and jurisdiction with zone, status, and expiry, or not-found, without personal details.
dataSent: Zone, status, and expiry date of a match, or a not-found result
interfaces.errorBehavior: Not-found is a normal result and is not an Active permit. A lookup date after the expiry date is not an Active result.
interfaces.representation: Deferred to design under CON-003. The source forbade inventing the wire format. Business content is FR-015, FR-019, and FR-020.

interfaces.name: City single sign-on for clerks
interfaces.purpose: Start a parking-clerk session only when the group parking-clerk is asserted.
dataReceived: Assertion of the group parking-clerk, or its absence
interfaces.errorBehavior: If the group is not asserted, a parking-clerk session does not start.
interfaces.representation: The source names the city single sign-on and the group claim. Token format and protocol were not specified and are deferred to design.

dataEntities.name: Application
dataEntities.description: One resident request for one vehicle, from drafting through a clerk decision.

attributes.name: legal name
attributes.meaning: The resident's legal name recorded on the application.

attributes.name: residential street address
attributes.meaning: The address compared to the eligible-address list.

attributes.name: email address
attributes.meaning: The address that receives CityNotify mail for this application and that receives the one-time link at sign-in.

attributes.name: license plate
attributes.meaning: The single plate named on the application.

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.meaning: The state or province of that plate.

attributes.name: zone
attributes.meaning: The ordinance zone the application is for.

attributes.name: status
attributes.meaning: Draft while the resident is filling it in, Submitted on the queue, Approved or Rejected after a clerk decision.

attributes.name: submission time
attributes.meaning: The time the application became Submitted, in UTC.

attributes.name: rejection reason
attributes.meaning: The clerk's reason, present when status is Rejected, at least 15 characters.

dataEntities.name: ProofOfAddressFile
dataEntities.description: The single file required before submission.

attributes.name: media type
attributes.meaning: The file kind the sponsor allowed.

attributes.name: size
attributes.meaning: The file size. Submission requires it to be no greater than 10 megabytes.

attributes.name: owning application
attributes.meaning: The application the file belongs to.

dataEntities.name: Permit
dataEntities.description: The permission issued after approval and successful payment, including a renewal's new permit.

attributes.name: permit number
attributes.meaning: A number the portal has not issued before.

attributes.name: status
attributes.meaning: Active at issuance. Suspended or Revoked only with a listed reason code. A lookup does not report Active after the expiry date even if the stored status is still Active.

attributes.name: issue date
attributes.meaning: The calendar date the permit was issued.

attributes.name: expiry date
attributes.meaning: The calendar date 365 days after the issue date.

attributes.name: zone
attributes.meaning: The zone on the issued permit.

attributes.name: license plate
attributes.meaning: The plate on the permit.

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.meaning: The plate jurisdiction on the permit.

attributes.name: email address
attributes.meaning: The email a resident must authenticate with to start a renewal of this permit.

attributes.name: legal name
attributes.meaning: Prefilled onto a renewal. Not returned on a plate lookup.

attributes.name: residential street address
attributes.meaning: Prefilled onto a renewal. Not returned on a plate lookup.

dataEntities.name: ZoneFee
dataEntities.description: The current ordinance amount for a zone.

attributes.name: zone
attributes.meaning: R-A or R-B on the current card, or a later zone supplied as data.

attributes.name: current amount

dataEntities.description: One street address on the cleaned list Parking Services supplies for a zone.

attributes.name: zone
attributes.meaning: The zone the list entry belongs to.

attributes.name: street address
attributes.meaning: The cleaned address text the application is compared to.

dataEntities.name: Payment
dataEntities.description: The record of what CityPay reported for an application.

attributes.name: application
attributes.meaning: The application the payment is for.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.meaning: The amount CityPay reported, present on success.

attributes.name: reference

attributes.name: outcome

attributes.name: recipient
attributes.meaning: The email address on the application.

attributes.name: attempt count
attributes.meaning: How many times this event was sent. The cap is 3.

attributes.name: accepted
attributes.meaning: Whether CityNotify accepted the message.

dataEntities.name: AuditRecord
dataEntities.description: The record appended for each approval, rejection, issuance, suspension, and revocation.

attributes.name: time
attributes.meaning: When the action was recorded, in UTC.

attributes.name: action

attributes.name: reason or payment reference

glossary.definition: The permit status at issuance. A lookup reports Active only under FR-015.
The clerk decision that moves a Submitted application to Approved.
The city's existing mail relay for the submission, rejection, and issuance emails. It is not stated to carry the one-time sign-in link.
The city's existing card processor. It hosts the page where the resident enters the card.
The ordinance amount for the application's zone at the moment the resident is sent to pay.
An application the resident is still filling in. It is not on the clerk queue.
The cleaned list of street addresses Parking Services supplies for a zone. Comparison is exact against that list. Fuzzy matching is out.
The state or province of a license plate.
The lookup result when no permit matches the plate and jurisdiction. It is not an Active permit.
The session started only when city single sign-on asserts the group parking-clerk.
The single file on an application. The sponsor also says proof of address. PDF, JPEG, or PNG, no larger than 10 megabytes.
The clerk decision on a Submitted application when a reason of at least 15 characters is recorded.
A permit status a clerk sets from Active with a listed reason code. A lookup does not report it as Active.
An application accepted onto the clerk review queue, with the submission time in UTC.
A permit status a clerk sets from Active with a listed reason code. A lookup does not report it as Active.
An ordinance parking area. The current card names R-A Residential Core at 60 US dollars a year and R-B Waterfront at 90 US dollars a year.

openQuestions.question: How many Active permits may one household hold?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: A cap would be a new eligibility rule. The sponsor said no number exists.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: Any number of permits per household, and any shall that limits or grants a household cap.
openQuestions.answerableBy: Dana Okonkwo, the sponsor. She said the policy is not written.

openQuestions.question: Which record produces the cleaned eligible-address list, and how often will Parking Services refresh it?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: An upstream interface or a freshness shall would depend on this answer.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: Any integration to a tax roll, utility account, or other system of record, and any refresh interval.
openQuestions.answerableBy: Dana Okonkwo. She said she does not yet know.

openQuestions.question: How long must a proof-of-address file be kept?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: A retention or deletion shall cannot be tested without a period.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: Any retention period, deletion date, or archive rule for the file.
openQuestions.answerableBy: The sponsor said Legal has not answered and named no person. Dana Okonkwo is the person who can bring that answer into the request.

openQuestions.question: What response time is required for resident page tasks, and how many applications arrive in a peak hour?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The only quantified performance target in the source is the plate lookup.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: Any page-response budget or application-volume figure.
openQuestions.answerableBy: Dana Okonkwo. She stated that she did not have these figures.

openQuestions.question: How quickly must the portal be restored after an unplanned outage?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: POL-AVAIL-03 as cited sets monthly availability and planned-maintenance notice, not a restore time.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: Any restore-time target or unplanned-outage procedure.

openQuestions.question: Who is allowed to request the monthly zone totals?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: FR-016 states the figures and names no actor, because the source names none.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: Any role, including clerk or sponsor, as the only party allowed to request the report.
openQuestions.answerableBy: Dana Okonkwo. BRD §6.14 records that this was not discussed.

openQuestions.question: Which channel sends the resident's one-time sign-in link?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: CityNotify is mandated for three other emails. The sign-in link is a separate send, and the source does not name its channel.
openQuestions.mustNotBeInvented: A decision that the link uses CityNotify, or a second mail product.

qualityModelCoverage.rationale: Functional suitability is specified by the functional requirements. Those statements are not copied again as non-functional requirements.
Lookup time-behaviour is specified. Resident-page time and capacity were not stated and stay in OQ-004. No target was invented for them.

Interoperability is the sourced behavior with CityPay, CityNotify, city single sign-on, and the handheld lookup. Co-existence with another named product on the same host was not required and is not applicable.
The 2011 name is usability. The sponsor's cited obligations are the 360 CSS pixel tasks and WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
Availability is the cited monthly percentage. Recoverability after an unplanned outage was not stated and is OQ-005.
Confidentiality, accountability, and authenticity are the sourced obligations. No cipher, vault, or token format was added.
The sponsor stated no analysability, modifiability, testability, or reuse target. No maintainability index was invented. This is not a design standard imported from outside the source.
The 2011 name is portability. Adaptability covers the cited browser matrix and the requirement that fees and the address list change without a software release.
The portal does not control vehicles, barriers, or signals. A wrong permit status is specified as functional correctness and confidentiality, not as the safety characteristic.
